chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated: Ahmad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Barqi narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban and others, from al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

He said: 'Whoever concludes his fasting with a virtuous word or a virtuous deed, Allah will accept his fasting.' He was asked: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the virtuous word?' He replied: 'The virtuous word is bearing witness that there is no god but Allah, and the virtuous deed is giving the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast).'

key_terms.إِخْرَاجُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Giving the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes the virtuous word and deed that ensure the acceptance of fasting?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual efficacy of concluding Ramadan with the Shahadah and paying Fitrah, linking ritual purity with theological affirmation. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating verbal declaration with tangible charitable acts to ensure the acceptance of worship. The specific mention of Fitrah reflects the jurisprudential tradition of purifying one's wealth and self at the close of the fasting month.
